chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Friday has a right and a sanctity, so beware of wasting or being deficient in anything from the worship of Allah and drawing near to Him through righteous deeds and abandoning all prohibitions, for Allah multiplies the good deeds therein, erases the bad deeds therein, and raises the ranks therein.

He said, and he mentioned that its day is like its night. So if you are able to spend it in prayer and supplication, then do so, for your Lord descends on the first part of the night of Friday to the lowest heaven, and He multiplies the good deeds therein and erases the bad deeds therein, and indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual merits and recommended acts of worship for Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a cornerstone of Shia devotional practice, emphasizing that Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) and its preceding night (Laylat al-Jumu'ah) are distinct periods of divine grace where the Almighty descends to the lowest heaven. This narrative underscores the theological concept of 'tad'if al-ahsanat' (multiplication of rewards), linking the physical act of worship with the spiritual imperative of preserving the sanctity of the day through both righteous deeds and abstention from prohibitions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammd, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For the Friday there is a right and a sanctity, therefore beware of wasting or being deficient regarding anything from the worship of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and getting closer to Him<sup>azwj</sup> with the righteous deeds and neglecting the Prohibitions, all of them, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Multiplies the good deeds therein, and Deletes the sins during it, and Raises the Levels during it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And heasws mentioned that its day is like its night. So if you have the capacity that you spend (all night) in offering the Salāt and the supplications, then do so, as (angels) descends from your Lordazwj during the beginning of the night of Friday from the sky to the world, and Heazwj Multiplies the good deeds during it and Deletes the sins during it, and that Allahazwj Kindness is Vast and Graceful’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

For Friday there are rights and respect, you must not fail to observe them or have shortcomings in worshipping Allah or in striving to become nearer to Him through good deeds and through refraining from all prohibited matters. Allah on this day increases good deeds, obliterates bad deeds and raises degrees of excellence.’

The narrator has said that the Imam then said, ‘Friday night is like its day. If you can, stay awake all night in Salah (prayer) and supplication; your Lord in the beginning of Friday night (commands an angel who) descends to the first heaven, (he) increases good deeds, obliterates bad deeds and Allah’s kindness is vast and graceful.’”
